Question B-006-005-007.

Why the correct answer is right: SWR describes the match by comparing forward and reflected waves at the measurement point; faults and loss can affect the reading. The correct choice, "standing waves are produced in the transmission line", is the option that matches this principle.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "standing waves are produced in the transmission line": Correct. SWR describes the match by comparing forward and reflected waves at the measurement point; faults and loss can affect the reading. The correct choice, "standing waves are produced in the transmission line", is the option that matches this principle.
- sourceIndex 1: "heat is produced at the junction": A mismatch creates standing waves; it does not automatically make SWR perfect or stop all radiation.
- sourceIndex 2: "the SWR reading falls to 1:1": A mismatch creates standing waves; it does not automatically make SWR perfect or stop all radiation.
- sourceIndex 3: "the antenna will not radiate any signal": A mismatch creates standing waves; it does not automatically make SWR perfect or stop all radiation.
